# Pattern catalogue

Each entry states a problem, at least three solutions, diagrams, tested implementations, measured comparisons and integration notes.

## Comparison across all implemented solutions

| Problem | Solution | One-line summary | Use when | Avoid when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Agent execution loops | [ReAct (interleaved reason, act, observe)](execution-loops/README.md#react-interleaved-reason-act-observe) | One model call per tool call. The model sees every observation before choosing the next action. | Short tasks, exploratory tasks, or unknown task shape | Long tasks where token cost matters |
| Agent execution loops | [Plan-and-Execute with symbolic references](execution-loops/README.md#plan-and-execute-with-symbolic-references) | One call writes the whole plan with placeholders for values not yet known; code executes it and calls the model again only when a step fails. | Task shape is predictable | Highly exploratory tasks where each observation changes what to do next |
| Agent execution loops | [Verified state-machine loop](execution-loops/README.md#verified-state-machine-loop) | An explicit graph (plan, execute, verify, repair) that refuses to run any side-effecting call until upstream steps and the call itself pass an independent check. | Side effects are expensive or irreversible | Read-only tasks |
| Multi-agent orchestration | [Single agent (baseline)](orchestration/README.md#single-agent-baseline) | One loop, one context, all tools. The option every multi-agent design must beat. | The task fits comfortably in one context | Context or latency limits are binding |
| Multi-agent orchestration | [Supervisor with isolated specialist workers](orchestration/README.md#supervisor-with-isolated-specialist-workers) | A supervisor decomposes once; code schedules subtasks onto workers as inputs become ready. Each worker gets a brief, its own tools and a fresh context, and returns condensed facts. | Subtasks are independent and can be specified in a short brief | Subtasks share subtle context that a brief would lose |
| Multi-agent orchestration | [Peer-to-peer handoff](orchestration/README.md#peer-to-peer-handoff) | No coordinator. The active specialist works until the next step is outside its tools, then transfers the conversation, whole, to a peer. | One conversation that changes hands (triage to specialist) | Many alternations between skills |
| Durable execution and checkpointing | [Restart from scratch](durable-execution/README.md#restart-from-scratch) | Persist nothing. After a crash, run the task again. | Read-only or fully idempotent tasks that are cheap to repeat | Anything with non-idempotent side effects |
| Durable execution and checkpointing | [Snapshot checkpointing](durable-execution/README.md#snapshot-checkpointing) | After each step (or graph node) write the whole state under a thread id; on restart load the latest snapshot and continue. | The loop is already a state graph | State is large and steps are frequent |
| Durable execution and checkpointing | [Event-sourced journal with deterministic replay](durable-execution/README.md#event-sourced-journal-with-deterministic-replay) | Record every model response and tool result in an append-only journal. After a crash re-run the same code; recorded results are returned without touching the model or the world. | You want durability as a wrapper | The loop is non-deterministic in ways you cannot record (wall-clock branches, unrecorded randomness) |
| Durable execution and checkpointing | [Idempotency keys on side effects (orthogonal, required)](durable-execution/README.md#idempotency-keys-on-side-effects-orthogonal-required) | Give every side-effecting call a key derived from the logical operation, so the backend applies it at most once however many times it is sent. | Always, for non-idempotent tools | Never; if the backend has no keys, add a read-back check before retrying |
| Tool registries and capability routing | [Static registry](tool-registry/README.md#static-registry) | Every tool is always exposed. Calls go straight to the backend. | Small, stable tool sets | Catalogues of dozens of tools |
| Tool registries and capability routing | [Capability-scoped registry with schema validation](tool-registry/README.md#capability-scoped-registry-with-schema-validation) | Expose only tools in the capability domains granted to this agent or task; reject calls that violate the schema before execution. Scopes can only narrow. | Known task types | Open-ended assistants that may need anything |
| Tool registries and capability routing | [Lazy discovery (tool search)](tool-registry/README.md#lazy-discovery-tool-search) | Expose one search tool. The model asks for a capability; matching schemas are loaded into context for the rest of the run. | Very large or changing catalogues | Few tools |
| Context and memory management | [Full history](context-memory/README.md#full-history) | Send everything every time. | Short and medium tasks | Runs that approach the context window |
| Context and memory management | [Sliding window](context-memory/README.md#sliding-window) | Keep the goal and the last N messages. | Chat-like interactions where old turns truly stop mattering | Tasks with long-range dependencies |
| Context and memory management | [Compaction (summarise and continue)](context-memory/README.md#compaction-summarise-and-continue) | When the context passes a threshold, replace older messages with a model-written summary and keep the most recent ones verbatim. | Long conversational or free-text runs | Exact values from early steps are needed later and are not in a ledger |
| Context and memory management | [Structured fact ledger](context-memory/README.md#structured-fact-ledger) | The runtime copies each tool result into a keyed ledger outside the transcript and shows the model the ledger plus the last few messages. | Tool outputs are structured | The valuable content is unstructured reasoning |
| Failure handling and retries | [Model-mediated retry](failure-recovery/README.md#model-mediated-retry) | Return the error as the observation and let the model decide to call again. | Validation and semantic errors | Infrastructure faults |
| Failure handling and retries | [Runtime retry with exponential backoff and jitter](failure-recovery/README.md#runtime-retry-with-exponential-backoff-and-jitter) | A wrapper under the model retries retryable errors on idempotent calls with capped, jittered delays. | Transient errors on idempotent calls | Long outages (add a breaker) |
| Failure handling and retries | [Circuit breaker with fallback](failure-recovery/README.md#circuit-breaker-with-fallback) | After repeated failures stop calling the dependency for a cool-down, route to a fallback if there is one, then probe. | Dependencies that can be down for minutes | Single-shot scripts |
| Failure handling and retries | [Idempotency keys for ambiguous outcomes](failure-recovery/README.md#idempotency-keys-for-ambiguous-outcomes) | Derive a key from the logical operation and send it with every side-effecting call, so a repeat after a lost reply is collapsed by the backend. | Every non-idempotent tool | Pure reads |
| Model selection and routing | [Static model](model-routing/README.md#static-model) | One model for every call. | Starting out | Cost matters and a failure signal is available |
| Model selection and routing | [Role-based routing](model-routing/README.md#role-based-routing) | Strong model for rare, high-leverage calls (plan, verify); cheap model for frequent ones (act). | Loops with distinct planner / verifier / executor roles | Single-role loops |
| Model selection and routing | [Cascade (escalate on evidence of failure)](model-routing/README.md#cascade-escalate-on-evidence-of-failure) | Run on the cheap model; switch to the strong model for a call when the latest context shows a failed tool call or a verifier rejection. | A verifier or loud tool errors exist | No failure signal |
| Permissions, approval and authorization | [Tool allowlist](permissions/README.md#tool-allowlist) | Only named tools exist for this agent. | Always, as the outer layer | As the only control on tools that take a destination |
| Permissions, approval and authorization | [Risk-tiered human approval with interrupt and resume](permissions/README.md#risk-tiered-human-approval-with-interrupt-and-resume) | Classify tools by effect. Reads run; risky tiers pause the run until a person approves or denies that exact call. | Irreversible, high-value or novel actions | High-frequency actions |
| Permissions, approval and authorization | [Attenuable capability tokens](permissions/README.md#attenuable-capability-tokens) | The agent holds a signed token listing tools, argument patterns, a call budget and an expiry. Any holder can narrow it; nobody can widen it. | Destinations and resources are known per task | Destinations are open-ended; use data-flow tracking instead |
| Execution tracing, observability and replay | [Flat event log](tracing-replay/README.md#flat-event-log) | Append one JSON object per model call, tool result, message and state transition. | Always | Never; restrict payloads if they hold sensitive data |
| Execution tracing, observability and replay | [Span tree (OpenTelemetry-shaped)](tracing-replay/README.md#span-tree-opentelemetry-shaped) | Fold events into parent/child spans with start, end, status and GenAI attribute names. | You already operate a tracing backend | As the only record; spans are a lossy projection |
| Execution tracing, observability and replay | [Record/replay tape](tracing-replay/README.md#recordreplay-tape) | Serve recorded model responses and tool results back to the same code, checking that each request matches the recording. | Debugging | Evaluating a prompt or model change (the recording no longer applies) |

To add an entry see [`docs/extending.md`](../docs/extending.md).
